# xfo-miner v1.0.11

This release adds an XMRig reject-rate watchdog so miners recover automatically when a pool rejects too many submitted shares.

## Highlights

- Monitors the configured local XMRig output log for share summary lines such as `rejected (566/3780)`.
- Restarts XMRig when the parsed reject ratio is greater than 10% after at least 20 total shares.
- Preserves the active XMRig mode (`full` or `heartbeat`) and configured thread count during watchdog restarts.
- Uses generation-scoped monitoring so stale XMRig processes cannot trigger restarts after a normal mode switch or shutdown.

## Scope

### XMRig high reject-rate recovery

- `internal/scheduler/xmrig.go` now starts a reject-rate monitor with each XMRig process generation.
- The monitor periodically reads `cpu_mining.xmrig_log_path`, parses the latest accepted/rejected summary, and restarts only when the rejection rate is strictly above 10%.
- Log read failures are reported as warnings without stopping the miner manager loop.
- The restart path reuses the existing XMRig lifecycle manager, preserving HTTP/API fallback behavior and process cleanup semantics.

## Validation

- Verified with:
  - `gofmt -w cmd/xfo-miner/main.go internal/scheduler/xmrig.go internal/scheduler/xmrig_test.go`
  - `go test ./...`
  - `go vet ./...`
  - `go build ./cmd/xfo-miner`
  - `git --no-pager diff --check -- cmd/xfo-miner/main.go internal/scheduler/xmrig.go internal/scheduler/xmrig_test.go`

## Operator notes

- CPU mining must have `cpu_mining.xmrig_log_path` configured or use the default generated by `config.json` loading.
- Existing XMRig logs are still rotated and retained by the local log management code.
- A reject rate of exactly 10% does not trigger a restart; the threshold is strictly greater than 10%.
